answer: A mesa bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every new agent must lock a stake on a high plateau that vests only after a season of verified useful work in the shared meadow, so spinning up a thousand clones means a thousand locked bonds. A gale audit then sweeps the meadow at random, re-checking a sample of completed tasks; any agent whose claimed work fails the re-check loses its bond and its grazing credits, and its sponsor's stake is cut too. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a herd that survives both the slow vesting and the random gale costs more than the attack can earn.
